name: Deep Value Thesis1 — DFIN print-to-software crossover
thesis: Donnelley Financial (DFIN) screens like a dying print/compliance business, but roughly 47% of net sales is now software (Venue data room, ActiveDisclosure, Arc Suite) growing high-single to double digits while legacy print shrinks. Trailing optics are distorted by a one-time non-cash pension-settlement charge that pushed reported P/E far above the normalized ~11x. The bet is that as software mix crosses toward the company's 60% target, the market re-rates the multiple; meanwhile normalized free cash flow carries the position at roughly 10% per year. This is a fair-price 'paid to wait' position, not a mispricing edge, and the crossover engine (Venue) carries real deal-cycle sensitivity that must be watched.
